name: Reed switch (normally open, glass 2 x 14 mm)
description: A magnetic switch: two contacts in a glass tube close when a magnet comes near (a lid, a door, a cover with a small magnet glued in) and open when it goes away. Draws no current itself. Wire one lead to a GPIO set to INPUT_PULLUP and the other to GND: the pin reads LOW while the magnet is near. Its magnet_mm prop is how far the magnet is (the live slider; a test sets {"set": "reed1.magnet", "value": "away"}). Can wake a sleeping ESP32 (a GPIO / ext0 wake-up).

props.label: Magnet distance
props.description: How far the magnet's face is from the switch (on its axis). Closes at about 13 mm with the default 6 x 3 mm N35 magnet.

props.label: Magnet grade
props.description: NdFeB grade (or a ferrite fridge-style magnet), sets its remanence.

props.label: Pull-in field
props.description: Field at which the contacts close. Datasheets give ampere-turns (AT): a 10-15 AT glass reed closes at roughly 2 to 6 mT along its axis; measure yours with the magnet you use.

props.label: Drop-out / pull-in
props.description: The contacts open again below this share of the pull-in field (hysteresis).

footprint: THT glass reed, 2.0 mm diameter, 14 mm glass, axial leads (bend 2 mm or more from the glass)

bindings.description: Flux density at the switch from the magnet (mT).
Distance at which this magnet closes it (mm).
Times the contacts closed since the run started.

magnet_switch.source: the part's defaults: pull-in 4 mT, drop-out 0.6 x pull-in (10-15 AT glass reed, rough)

mechanical.source: typical 2 x 14 mm glass reed (e.g. MKA-14103 class); leads not counted
